content.title: About
content.content: An ice cream candy bar is a dessert that combines creamy ice cream with a crunchy chocolate coating. It often contains nuts, caramel, or fruit pieces inside. The format is portable, making it popular year‑round.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ice‑cream bar hit the U.S. market in the 1970s as an alternative to traditional cone ice cream.
Stabilizers are added to keep the ice cream firm during temperature fluctuations.
More than 30 flavor variations exist: vanilla, chocolate, strawberry, mint‑chocolate, and others.
Bars are frequently double‑coated with dark and milk chocolate for extra crunch.
In some countries the bars are sold in mini‑size portions for children.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The dairy base provides a notable amount of calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B2 and B12 vitamins in the milk support energy metabolism.

items.title: Small amount of protein
items.content: Milk protein contributes to tissue repair.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The bar delivers fast‑acting calories, useful during active days.

items.title: Mood boost
items.content: Sweet taste can improve mood and reduce stress.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may lead to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should choose dairy‑free versions.

items.title: Nut and gluten allergies
items.content: Some bars contain nuts, peanuts, or wheat crumbs, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Melting in heat
items.content: Storing in hot environments can cause the bar to melt and lose its texture.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bar straight from the wrapper, optionally letting it soften for a few minutes. It can be chopped and added to ice cream, yogurt, or used as a topping for desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once removed from the freezer, consume within 2–3 days to prevent ice crystal formation.

pizza-with-meat-and-vegetables-from-froz.title: Pizza with meat and vegetables, frozen, medium crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with meat and vegetables is a ready‑to‑cook frozen product featuring a medium‑thick crust, tomato sauce, assorted meats (ham, sausage, beef) and fresh vegetables (bell pepper, onion, mushrooms). It is designed for quick oven preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frozen pizzas preserve the flavor and nutrients of ingredients for long periods.
A medium crust offers a balance between crispiness and softness.
The meat‑vegetable combination provides a more balanced source of protein and fiber.
Tomato sauce contains lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Pizza is often used as a fast dinner or snack when time is limited.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Meat ingredients supply complete proteins essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomato sauce and vegetables provide vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Vegetables add dietary fiber, aiding digestion and promoting satiety.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The crust delivers carbohydrates for quick energy.

items.title: Convenient preparation
items.content: The frozen product cooks in 10‑15 minutes, saving time.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salt used in the sauce and meat can be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Meat components may contain saturated fats, which should be limited in cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain gluten, dairy, and soy, important for individuals with those allergies.

items.title: Need for thorough heating
items.content: Insufficiently heated pizza may harbor bacteria, so follow the recommended temperature.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Place the pizza on a baking sheet or rack and bake for 10‑15 minutes until the crust is golden. Let it cool slightly before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen pizza at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, use within 24 hours and do not keep at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

potato-salad-with-egg-made-with-light-ma.title: Potato Salad with Egg, Light Mayonnaise Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad with boiled eggs dressed with a light mayonnaise sauce is a classic dish of Russian cuisine. The potatoes and eggs provide heartiness, while the light dressing adds a gentle flavor without excess fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The salad is often served at festive tables, especially during the summer months.
A light mayonnaise dressing is usually made from egg yolks, vegetable oil, mustard, and a small amount of vinegar or lemon juice.
Traditional recipes may include fresh dill or green onions for extra aroma.
Potatoes are typically boiled in their skins to retain shape and texture.
The salad keeps its taste for 3‑4 days when stored in the refrigerator.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Potatoes contain vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potatoes supply potassium, important for blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The light mayonnaise dressing has less saturated fat than regular mayo, making the salad more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in potatoes helps maintain normal bowel function.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Excessive salt in the dressing can contribute to hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Salads containing boiled eggs should be refrigerated and not left at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even with a light dressing, the salad is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish or as a side to meat or fish. Garnish with fresh herbs, add a dash of mustard, or a spoonful of sour cream to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Consume within 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato paste is a ready‑to‑eat product made by cooking or baking sweet potatoes (batata) and pureeing them into a smooth, creamy consistency. It has a gentle sweet flavor, velvety texture, and bright orange color. The paste is convenient for use as a base in dishes, in baking, as baby food, or enjoyed on its own as a dessert.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Unlike regular potatoes, sweet potatoes contain less starch and more natural sugars, giving them a sweeter taste.
Sweet potato paste is a staple in Caribbean, African, and Asian cuisines.
Sweet potatoes can be cultivated in a wider range of climates than regular potatoes.
It is considered a hypoallergenic food and is often included in infant menus.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C enhances antioxidant protection and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Moderate glycemic impact after cooking
items.content: Sweet potato paste has a gentler glycemic response compared with regular potato, making it suitable for moderate consumption by people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergy to sweet potato
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to sweet potato.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The natural sweetness means people monitoring sugar intake should account for it in their overall diet.

items.title: Contamination if stored improperly
items.content: Storing the paste in warm, humid conditions can lead to rapid spoilage and bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sweet potato paste can be enjoyed as a standalone dessert, mixed into smoothies, yogurts, oatmeal, used as a filling for pies, pancakes, dumplings, or as a base for sauces and soups. It reheats well in the microwave or on the stove, optionally thinned with milk or a plant‑based beverage for a smoother consistency.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the paste in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags – it retains flavor and nutrients for up to 3 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or visible mold; discard if any signs of spoilage are present.
